about: Every engine name the Unreal seed (unreal/) and the stand-ins its tests compile it against (tests/tools/unreal-standin/) assume, each checked against Epic's public documentation, or, for a rule of the C++ language itself, against the C++20 working draft. The seed has never been built by the engine; this register says how far the public record supports each assumption, and what only a build can settle.
reference: Epic's documentation at dev.epicgames.com: the guides of the current version, and the C++ API reference of Unreal Engine 5.8, or of 5.5 and 5.7 where the 5.8 page leaves a detail out. The seed targets Unreal Engine 5.9, whose API reference was not published when this was checked. The reference prints signatures without default arguments, does not document macros, and drops a trailing const in its class tables. Epic's engine source is not public, so no header was read. Where an assumption is a rule of the C++ language rather than of the engine, it is checked against the C++20 working draft (N4861, in the cplusplus/draft repository on GitHub), the standard Epic's coding standard says the engine builds with.

statuses.verified: The quoted passage, on the page named, states or shows what is assumed: the name and, for a function, its parameters or the behaviour relied on.
statuses.partly: The name is documented but something the seed or a stand-in relies on is not: a default argument, a value's spelling, an include that brings a name in.
statuses.unverified: No public page was found that shows it.

symbols.assumes: The character type of TEXT() literals, of FString characters and of const TCHAR* parameters, and a wide one: the stand-in makes it wchar_t, so a narrow string passed where TCHARs are wanted does not compile.

source.title: Character Encoding in Unreal Engine | Unreal Engine 5.9 Documentation | Epic Developer Community

symbols.passage: All strings in UE are stored in memory in UTF-16 format as FStrings or TCHAR arrays.
symbols.note: The API reference gives TCHAR as "Either ANSICHAR or WIDECHAR, depending on whether the platform supports wide characters or the requirements of the licensee" (Core module page), and the coding standard says never to assume its size. The seed does not: it handles text only through TEXT, FString and FName. On the Linux machines that run the stand-in build, wchar_t is 32 bits rather than 16; what the stand-in checks is that narrow and wide strings are not mixed.

symbols.assumes: TEXT("...") wraps a string literal so that it is a TCHAR literal.

source.title: Unreal Engine UProperties | Unreal Engine 5.9 Documentation | Epic Developer Community

symbols.passage: For most uses, Unreal relies on the TCHAR type for characters. The TEXT() macro is available to denote TCHAR literals.
symbols.note: States what the macro is for. The coding standard page adds "Always use the TEXT() macro around string literals."

symbols.symbol: TEXT literal as inline constexpr const TCHAR*
symbols.assumes: A TEXT("...") literal can initialise a namespace-scope `inline constexpr const TCHAR*` constant and an array of them: TEXT gives a string literal (entry TEXT), a string literal is an object with static storage duration, and the address of such an object may be the value of a constant expression.

source.title: C++20 working draft N4861, [expr.const] (cplusplus/draft, source/expressions.tex)

symbols.passage: if the value is of pointer type, it contains the address of an object with static storage duration
symbols.note: A rule of the language, not of the engine, so it is checked against the C++20 working draft: Epic's coding standard says "Unreal Engine compiles with a language version of C++20 by default and requires a minimum version of C++20 to build." The other half is [lex.string] (source/lex.tex of the same draft): evaluating a string literal "results in a string literal object with static storage duration, initialized from the given characters as specified above". The stand-in build compiles TervainIds.h in this form as C++20.
